parsed.rationale: Although both `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` and `AudioPlayerProtocol` live in the same `Playback` package and share a handful of method names (`installRenderTap`, `removeRenderTap`, `isPlaying`, `stop`, `play`), the structural evidence explicitly reports `shared_field_count: 0` and `jaccard: null`, indicating the pipeline found no formally shared slots. More importantly, the two protocols diverge in semantically meaningful ways: `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` exposes `scheduleBuffer`, `scheduleBuffers`, `makeRenderTapStream`, `volume`, and a `play:() throws` signature, while `AudioPlayerProtocol` exposes `state:PlayerState`, `stateStream:AsyncStream<PlayerState>`, `makeAudioBufferStream`, and a non-throwing `play:()`. These differences suggest the two protocols model distinct abstraction layers (a low-level AVAudioEngine scheduling surface vs. a higher-level stateful player interface) whose structural overlap is coincidental rather than a sign of a missing parent protocol.
